facts.statement: The genus Chromogisaurus was first named by the paleontologist Martín Daniel Ezcurra in 2010.
facts.quote: Chromogisaurus was first named by Martín Daniel Ezcurra in 2010

facts.statement: The only known species in the genus is named Chromogisaurus novasi.
facts.quote: The type species is Chromogisaurus novasi

facts.statement: The genus name Chromogisaurus means "color of the earth" in Greek, referencing the Painted Valley where the fossils were found.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from Greek chroma, "colour", and gè, "earth", a reference to the Valle Pintado, the "Painted Valley".

facts.statement: The species name novasi honors the Argentine paleontologist Fernando Emilio Novas.
facts.quote: The specific name honours Fernando Emilio Novas.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen, cataloged as PVSJ 845, was discovered in the Cancha de Bochas Member of the Ischigualasto Formation.
facts.quote: The holotype, PVSJ 845, was found in the Cancha de Bochas Member of the Ischigualasto Formation, dating to the Carnian.

facts.statement: Chromogisaurus is considered one of the oldest known dinosaurs.
facts.quote: This makes Chromogisaurus one of the oldest known dinosaurs.

facts.statement: Chromogisaurus was a small herbivore that stood about 2 meters long.
facts.quote: It was a small, bipedal herbivore, about 2 m in length.

facts.statement: Chromogisaurus was an herbivore approximately 2 meters long that could walk on all fours.
facts.quote: Era un herbívoro de unos 2 metros de longitud, y era opcionalmente cuadrúpedo.

facts.statement: The fossil specimen is a partial skeleton missing the skull but including parts of the front and hind limbs, pelvis, and tail vertebrae.
facts.quote: The specimen consists of a partial skeleton lacking the skull, with elements of the front and hind limbs, as well as the pelvis and two caudal vertebrae.

facts.statement: Chromogisaurus is classified as an extinct genus of sauropodomorph dinosaur.
facts.quote: Chromogisaurus is an extinct genus of saturnaliid sauropodomorph

facts.statement: Cladistic analysis places Chromogisaurus within the basal sauropodomorph family Guaibasauridae.
facts.quote: A cladistic analysis by Ezcurra indicated that Chromogisaurus was a member of a clade basal sauropodomorphs, the Guaibasauridae

facts.statement: Within the family Guaibasauridae, Chromogisaurus forms a subfamily called Saturnaliinae with its sister taxon Saturnalia.
facts.quote: Dentro de Guaibasauridae forma un clado más pequeño con su taxón hermano Saturnalia, la subfamilia Saturnaliinae.

facts.statement: Chromogisaurus lived in South America about 220 million years ago during the Carnian age of the Late Triassic.
facts.quote: vivió a finales del período Triásico, hace aproximadamente 220 millones de años en el Carniense en lo que es hoy Sudamérica.

facts.statement: The time range for Chromogisaurus is estimated between 237 and 227.3 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Carnian to Carnian (237 to 227.3 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Chromogisaurus lived in Argentina during the Late Triassic period.
rejected.quote: It existed in Argentina during the Late Triassic (Carnian) period.
